translations.t0035: Rochat claims to have been in office 2F-4 until approximately 22:30 CEST on Friday 10.10. and to have driven directly to Bern afterwards.
translations.t0036: The garage log shows exit at 21:28 system time = 22:28 CEST (confirmed +1h correction). Card payments at Raststätte Thurau 22:47 CEST and Raststätte Würenlos 23:29 CEST confirm a westbound journey on the A1. Würenlos is approximately 60 km from St. Gallen; the payment falls within the offence window but places Rochat physically on the motorway. June Okada's statement places Rochat's music on the 2nd floor at around 20:00 and no further person thereafter, which is consistent with a departure at ~22:28.
translations.t0037: Rochat claims to have driven to Bern and spent the night at her sister's there (night of 10./11.10.).
translations.t0038: There is no card payment, hotel record, or witness statement that positively establishes her presence in Bern on the night of 10./11.10. A private overnight stay at her sister's would leave no payment trace. The expense report REIMB-2025-10-109 confirms the context ('Sat 11 Oct drove to Bern for the product offsite venue visit, back Mon') and was submitted before the investigation, which indicates no retrospective attempt at construction. A card payment on the return journey at Würenlos eastbound on 13.10. is consistent with 'back Mon'.
translations.t0039: Rochat claims to have visited the venue on Gurten on Monday 13.10.
translations.t0040: The venue visit task is supported by email correspondence (offsite planning, Gurten on the shortlist) and the calendar entry 'Leave early – drive to Bern / Venue visit for the spring offsite'. The return card payment at Würenlos eastbound on 13.10. at 17:05 CEST is consistent with returning from Bern on Monday. A direct confirmation of her presence at Gurten on 13.10. is missing.
translations.t0041: Rochat claims to have been at the Rosenbergstrasse premises for her interview on Friday 21.11. (from 12:00).
translations.t0042: The garage log shows entry of TI 88 402 on 21.11. at 13:55 system time. As the clock discrepancy had been corrected from 26.10. onward, this corresponds to approximately 13:55 CET — consistent with returning after the interview. The interview began at 12:03 at an external location.
translations.t0043: Rochat demonstrably had access to two of the three critical knowledge elements: (1) Real/Decoy Mapping (Slide 11) via the Q1 Board Pack (she was on the distribution list as presenting executive); (2) basic awareness of the decoy's existence via the Confluence page. She had no documented access to the undocumented staging path (K2): she is not among the persons listed by Andrin Caduff as knowing it ('Lukas, Iris, Yannick, people from before 2023'), has no engineering background, and Lukas Hofer explicitly ruled out that the diligence data room revealed the path. Whether Rochat knew the staging path remains open. Without this knowledge, a targeted exfiltration would be difficult to carry out.
translations.t0044: Rochat works on the 2nd floor in office 2F-4. The scene of the offence is the engineering floor (workstation console). There is no established evidence that Rochat had access to the workstation on the engineering floor or could operate the scratch arrays. She has no engineering role. According to Andrin Caduff, the Alley-Door was regularly open, which facilitates physical access without a badge — but this applies to all persons.
translations.t0045: Rochat's vehicle left the garage at 22:28 CEST. Card payments place her at 22:47 CEST in Thurau (Wil SG) and at 23:29 CEST in Würenlos — concurrent with the offence start at 23:10 CEST. From 23:29 CEST onward she was physically approximately 60 km from St. Gallen. The exfiltration continued until 05:58 CEST; there is no evidence of a return to St. Gallen that night.
translations.t0046: Rochat was on the distribution list for the Q1 Board Pack (Slide 11, Real/Decoy Mapping by path) and demonstrably read the Confluence page. She therefore possessed knowledge (K1) that, according to Iris Ammann, was supposed to be accessible only to a small circle.
translations.t0047: The undocumented staging path (K2) is the critical knowledge gap: Rochat is not among the persons who should have known it, has no engineering role, and Lukas Hofer ruled out that the diligence data room revealed this path. Without this knowledge, a targeted exfiltration would scarcely be possible.
translations.t0048: The 9 accounts that read the Confluence page are not documented by name. It cannot be excluded that Rochat's single access in April is among the 9 accounts, but it is likewise not established that she extracted the staging path information from it.
translations.t0049: The card payments (Thurau 22:47, Würenlos 23:29 CEST) place Rochat physically on the A1 towards Bern — concurrent with the offence start at 23:10 CEST. This constitutes strong exculpatory evidence for the offence period, corroborated by independent card data. S4 (detailed knowledge of the course of the offence) is convincingly explained by Arslan's speakerphone call on 20.11. The absence of evidence of staging path knowledge (K2) and the unidentifiable 9 Confluence accounts prevent a complete exoneration. Complete exoneration would be possible if Rochat's presence in Bern on the night of 10./11.10. were confirmed by an independent source (sister, Bern petrol receipt, etc.).
translations.t0050: Noemi Rochat is substantially exonerated by independent card payments on the A1 (22:47 and 23:29 CEST) during the start of the offence (23:10 CEST); her precise description of the offence is plausibly explained by the investigator's inadvertent speakerphone call on the preceding evening. The absence of evidence regarding the undocumented staging path and the unconfirmed overnight stay in Bern mean that suspicion cannot be entirely dispelled.
translations.t0051: The 9 Confluence accounts that read the storage-controls page are not documented by name; Rochat's access is confirmed, but the content of the information known to her (in particular the staging path) is unclear.
translations.t0052: The overnight stay in Bern (night of 10./11.10.) is not confirmed by any independent source; a private overnight stay at her sister's is plausible but leaves no trace.
translations.t0053: It has not been established whether Rochat had physical access to the workstation on the engineering floor or possessed the technical knowledge required for the exfiltration.
translations.t0054: The key knowledge K2 (undocumented staging path) is not documented in relation to Rochat; she could have learned it verbally, which cannot be excluded.
translations.t0055: The green Volvo estate with a roof box that June Okada saw in the garage after Rochat's departure could not be attributed to any vehicle owner — the person who was still in the building after 22:28 CEST remains unknown.
translations.t0056: Vogel assembled the Q1 Board Deck (February 2025) including Slide 11 (Real/Decoy assignment by path) and read all slides for formatting purposes. The slide was visually present before Iris Ammann ordered its removal.
translations.t0057: Vogel managed the four-month Kestrel diligence process and was the primary contact for Gilles Aubert. Data room service accounts were never revoked (SEC-419 open); the export role dr-export-ro had excessively broad read access to active staging trees since April.
translations.t0058: Vogel claims to have left the office on Friday 10 October at around 18:00 and arrived in Ascona alone at around 20:30–21:00. No witness for Friday evening. The first evidenced card payment on 11 October is at 07:52 CEST in St. Gallen (Coop Pronto Kreuzbleiche), which would be difficult to reconcile with a return from Ascona only on Monday — unless this payment was made on the outward journey or very early in the morning before continuing.
translations.t0059: Gilles Aubert offered Vogel a position on the Kestrel side in May 2025. Vogel forwarded this to Dov; the thread reads clean, but the contact existed.
translations.t0060: Vogel saw Slide 11 while formatting, before Iris Ammann ordered its removal on 5 February 2025. Vogel confirmed the deletion from the shared folder promptly. Crucially: Lukas Hofer confirmed in his interview that the diligence materials Vogel sent to Kestrel did not reveal where the real checkpoints are located — he had personally reviewed every dataset. Slide 11 alone would therefore have given Vogel the Decoy/Real Mapping, but not the undocumented staging path (K2), which was indispensable for the exfiltration. Furthermore, the Board itself resolved during the meeting to remove the slide; Vogel subsequently received Iris's written instruction and acted immediately.
translations.t0061: Iris Ammann instructed Vogel on 5 February 2025 to remove Slide 11 — immediately after the Board meeting.
translations.t0062: Vogel confirmed the removal within 28 minutes.
translations.t0063: Lukas Hofer confirms that the diligence documents did not reveal the staging path.
translations.t0064: The removal of Slide 11 was resolved at the Board meeting itself, not on Vogel's own initiative.
translations.t0065: Vogel acknowledges having seen all slides. Whether she understood the content of Slide 11 and retained the path remains open — her own statement suggests a lack of understanding of technical content, but does not prove it.
translations.t0066: The slide contained an explicit path mapping; even without understanding the file system, someone could have photographed or noted this content.
translations.t0067: Vogel was the data room owner in name, but technical provisioning lay with an external law firm (Brunner Keller) and internal infrastructure (Yannick Favre). According to her own account, Vogel had no visibility into the scope of access of the service accounts. The incorrect scoping of dr-export-ro was an infrastructure error made under time pressure in April, not an action by Vogel. The account was theoretically usable, but: the exfiltration was carried out from a local workstation console on the engineering floor — no network session, no remote access via the data room.
translations.t0068: According to her own account, Vogel had no knowledge of the scope of access of the service accounts.
translations.t0069: The exfiltration was a physical local action; remote access via data room accounts was not the attack path.
translations.t0070: Formal ownership with Vogel, operational provisioning with the law firm and infrastructure.
translations.t0071: The account with excessively broad read access to staging trees remained open; in theory, someone with knowledge of this account could have explored the path — but this attack path is not the one established by forensics.
translations.t0072: The card payment in St. Gallen on 11 October at 07:52 CEST (Coop Pronto Kreuzbleiche) is in tension with the claim of having been in Ascona throughout the night. There is, however, an innocent explanation: Vogel stated that she stayed in Ascona until Monday midday and returned home on Monday at ~19:00. The payment on Saturday morning at 07:52 in St. Gallen would then only be reconcilable if Vogel either (a) made a brief trip to St. Gallen and back early on Saturday morning — which would entail approximately 6 hours of driving and is implausible — or (b) the payment has an alternative explanation (e.g. another person used the card, which is not supported by the file). Against this: the Parking Ascona Lido records an entry on Saturday 11 October and an exit on Monday 13 October at 16:02. This presupposes that Vogel's vehicle was in Ascona from Saturday onward — which would only be reconcilable with a Saturday-morning payment in St. Gallen if the vehicle and the cardholder were not the same. The card payment is linked to Vogel's card, not to the vehicle.
translations.t0073: The Parking Ascona Lido records an entry on Saturday 11 October and an exit on Monday 13 October at 16:02.
translations.t0074: Vogel's card paid for the Parking Ascona Lido on 13 October (UTC 14:02 = CEST 16:02).
translations.t0075: Vogel's expense report describes departure on Friday evening and return on Monday 13 October.
translations.t0076: Further card payment on 11 October at 09:54 CEST at the Autogrill San Bernardino (A13, Mesocco) — located on the route St. Gallen–Ascona. This is consistent with an outward journey on Saturday, not with a return journey.
translations.t0077: Card payment at 07:52 CEST in St. Gallen on Saturday morning. If Vogel was in Ascona throughout Friday night, this payment is inexplicable without a return to St. Gallen or without an alternative explanation (third party using the card, which is not established).
translations.t0078: Vogel forwarded Aubert's email containing the job offer to Dov Halperin within 46 minutes and described it herself as 'leverage'. The investigator (NB-L72) confirms that this thread reads clean. The conduct is consistent with transparency.
translations.t0079: Vogel proactively informed the CEO within the hour.
translations.t0080: Investigator confirms: the thread reads clean.
translations.t0081: Vogel claims to have left the office on Friday 10 October at around 18:00.
translations.t0082: The out-of-office expired at 17:55 CEST, which is consistent with a departure at approximately 18:00. The garage log shows an entry on 10 October at 07:41 (SG 482 117), but no exit in the provided extract. June Okada's witness statement mentions that she left the office shortly before 21:00 and saw 'the usual green Volvo estate with a roof box' in the car park — which would mean Vogel's vehicle was still in the building at ~21:00.
translations.t0083: Vogel claims to have driven the route Motorway–Chur–San Bernardino–Bellinzona to Ascona on Friday 10 October, arriving at around 20:30–21:00.
translations.t0084: June Okada's witness statement places the green Volvo estate with a roof box (Vogel's vehicle per the parking permit) still in the car park shortly before 21:00. Given that the drive to Ascona takes approximately 3 hours, an arrival at 20:30–21:00 would be impossible if the departure was after 21:00. Furthermore, the garage log shows no exit in the extract. The witness statement is not independent (no camera, no licence-plate recognition for the exit), and the witness identifies the vehicle by type and colour only, not by registration plate. This is incriminating but not conclusive.
translations.t0085: Vogel claims to have been in Ascona throughout the night of 10 to 11 October.
translations.t0086: The card payment on 11 October at 07:52 CEST at Coop Pronto Kreuzbleiche in St. Gallen contradicts continuous presence in Ascona during that night. St. Gallen is approximately 3 hours from Ascona. A payment at 07:52 in St. Gallen is incompatible with a night spent in Ascona. However: a subsequent card payment at 09:54 CEST at the Autogrill San Bernardino (Mesocco, on the A13 between St. Gallen and Ascona) indicates a southbound journey. A possible reconstruction: Vogel was still in St. Gallen in the early hours of Saturday morning, then drove south and reached Ascona after the Autogrill stop. This would mean she was in or near St. Gallen during the offence window (23:10–05:58 CEST).
translations.t0087: Vogel claims to have returned home on Monday 13 October in the afternoon, arriving at approximately 19:00.
